short: This is not a motif family. It is a holding pen for small, thinly characterized factors that needed somewhere to go, and it currently holds eleven matrices for nine unrelated proteins: MSANTD1, MSANTD3 and MSANTD4, DNTTIP1, FLYWCH1, FAM200B, ELYS/AHCTF1, NACC2 and XPA. Internal cohesion is 0.47, the lowest of any group in this atlas. Two warnings about the label. The name mentions SCAN and SSX domains, but no SCAN-domain or SSX protein has a motif here; and BANP, named in the definition, is not here either - its only model sits in the other-BTB-zinc-finger bucket. XPA is the central scaffold of nucleotide excision repair, not a transcription factor. The motifs themselves are mostly well supported.
long:
## The factors

Nine proteins, eleven models, no shared biology; read the list, not the label, which mentions SCAN and SSX domains that are not represented.

BANP is named in the definition and is the most interesting protein in the set, but its motif is filed elsewhere. The CGCG element was for years an orphan promoter motif, enriched near the start sites of a subset of CpG-island promoters and associated with highly expressed genes; single-molecule footprinting combined with interaction proteomics identified BTG3-associated nuclear protein as its binder. Methylation of the motif repels BANP, confining it to unmethylated CpG islands, and on binding it opens chromatin, phases nucleosomes and activates essential metabolic genes. Structures of BEN domains later showed that oligomerization lets BANP select unmethylated CGCG. Here that motif rides on a Vierstra archetype with a joint ZBTB/BANP label, so it went to the other-BTB-zinc-finger entry instead.

The BEN domain reaches one protein that is here: of nine human BEN-domain proteins, NACC1 prefers CATG-containing sequence, and the NACC2 model here reads ACATGC. DNTTIP1, originally TdT-interacting factor 1, is a subunit of the mitotic deacetylase complex MiDAC; its C-terminal SKI/SNO/DAC-like domain binds DNA and nucleosomes, making it a chromatin-binding module rather than an activator. FLYWCH1 is a FLYWCH-type zinc finger studied as a suppressor of nuclear beta-catenin in colorectal cancer. FAM200B, also called ZBED11, is transposase-derived, of the hAT/ZBED lineage with an RNase H-like fold. MSANTD1, MSANTD3 and MSANTD4 carry Myb/SANT-like DNA-binding domains and almost no documented function. ELYS/AHCTF1 was named a transcription factor when cloned from mouse foetal haematopoietic tissue, then shown to be a nucleoporin that seeds Nup107-160 assembly and doubles as a kinetochore protein. XPA was cloned in 1990 as an excision-repair gene "containing a zinc-finger domain", which is how censuses of putative transcription factors caught it; it is the scaffold of nucleotide excision repair and reads splayed-arm junction geometry, not sequence.

## The motif

There is no consensus: the reported CACTCAc is only the MSANTD3 medoid of eleven unrelated matrices, and cohesion is 0.47.

HOCOMOCO v14 encodes assays in the model name: P is ChIP-seq, S HT-SELEX, M methyl-HT-SELEX, G genomic HT-SELEX, I SMiLE-seq, B protein-binding microarray, and grade A means at least two assay types agreed. Most are good on that scale. FLYWCH1 gives aTTCGAhcCGATTCGA, a 19-bit tandem TTCGA repeat, from PSGB at grade A. FAM200B gives the 13-bp palindrome TGGGTCGCGaCCC, 16 bits, PSGIB grade A, the shape a dimeric domesticated transposase should give. MSANTD4 gives acTTACTACtcg (13.8 bits, SGIB, A), MSANTD1 CACTTAAG (10.8 bits, PSGIB, A), DNTTIP1 GcatGCAC (PSG, A) and NACC2 ACATgc (PSGIB, A). Six of the seven HOCOMOCO models are grade A from up to five platforms, the assay set used by the recent systematic effort on poorly characterized human factors that produced motifs for 177 of 332 candidates. A protein with no literature can still have a well-measured motif.

Three entries are weaker. MSANTD3 appears twice, as JASPAR MA1523.2 and CIS-BP M01259, both reading CACTCAc and both flagged as resembling the NKX homeodomain family at 0.94-0.97, so that hexamer is not separable from an NKX site. ELYS contributes AAAT, 8.5 bits, from PBM alone at grade B, with a best match outside the bucket of 0.99: an AT-rich four-mer indistinguishable from any other AT-rich model. XPA appears twice, as CIS-BP M05827 and the Vierstra archetype AC0333:XPA:Unknown, whose domain label is literally "Unknown"; neither carries an assay label here.

## Where it acts

Unmapped for almost everything here; BANP, filed elsewhere, is the exception, at unmethylated CpG-island promoters near transcription start sites, with binding lost where those promoters are aberrantly methylated in cancer. For the rest, the systematic work on understudied factors found in vitro motifs enriched at cellular binding sites concentrated in promoters, making promoter-proximal the prior. Scan arithmetic matters more than location: ACATGC or CACTCA is expected several hundred thousand times per strand in 3.1 Gb and AAAT tens of millions of times, so the ELYS and MSANTD3 models cannot localise anything, while FLYWCH1's or FAM200B's long matrices are genuinely rare.

## Biology and disease

XPA is the only member with a Mendelian disease of its own, and it is a repair disease: biallelic mutations cause xeroderma pigmentosum group A, with extreme ultraviolet sensitivity and, in severe alleles, neurodegeneration. MiDAC, the complex DNTTIP1 assembles, is essential for mouse embryonic development. MSANTD3 appears as an HTN3-MSANTD3 fusion defining a subset of salivary acinic cell carcinoma. ELYS loss blocks nuclear pore assembly and chromosome segregation. MSANTD1, MSANTD4, FAM200B and NACC2 have no established disease link.

## Reading a hit

Name the matrix, not the family: a hit here is on one of eleven unrelated models. Then triage. If you came for the BANP motif, it is TCTCGCGAGA on archetype AC0312:ZBTB/BANP in the other-BTB-zinc-finger entry, and it matches the ZBTB33/Kaiso archetype at 0.99, so sequence alone will not say which of the two bound - use methylation state and expression. If the hit is XPA, discard it: XPA has no sequence specificity. If it is ELYS AAAT, discard it as AT-rich background. If it is MSANTD3 CACTCA, check the NKX entry first. If it is FLYWCH1, FAM200B, MSANTD1, MSANTD4, DNTTIP1 or NACC2, the matrix is reasonable evidence and the protein is not: treat the site as a candidate for an understudied factor, confirm the gene is expressed, and note that on structure FAM200B belongs with the ZBED entry and the MSANTD proteins with MYB.
caveats: This is an administrative holding pen, not a family. Eleven matrices for nine unrelated proteins, cohesion 0.47, the lowest in the atlas; there is no consensus and none should be quoted. The label misleads twice: no SCAN-domain or SSX protein has a motif here, and BANP, named in the definition, has its only model filed under other BTB-zinc-fingers as the joint ZBTB/BANP archetype. XPA is a nucleotide excision repair scaffold that binds DNA by shape, so its two models should not be scanned at all, and the ELYS model is a PBM-only AT-rich four-mer. Conversely, do not dismiss the whole group: six of the seven HOCOMOCO models are grade A from several independent assay platforms.
